attributes.residual: PARKED FOR SESSION BUDGET, NOT FOR A DEAD END - THIS IS AN OPEN, WELL-CHARACTERISED CANDIDATE AND THE NEXT AXIS IS NAMED. Baseline measurement: target frame 160 / ours 216, target low_gap 16 / ours 80, i.e. we over-reserve 64 bytes at the BOTTOM of the frame; every referenced slot is shifted (target 24/28/32/48/160/164 vs ours 88/92/96/104/216/220). Critically the opcode streams are already almost identical - insns 343 target / 342 ours with multiset 1t - so this function is a nearly pure frame/occupancy problem worth real effort, not a codegen rewrite. Two facts established this pass: (a) sfx.c has no static inline helpers, so our over-reservation is NOT the AudioWithName mechanism; (b) the existing `u8 _spare[8]` IS load-bearing (removing it moved the frame exactly 8 and left real flat at 191), so the pad is a usable byte reservoir and the someone_will_be_off_screen inert-pad trap does not apply here. NEXT AXIS, unstarted: StartExplosion declares a large number of INNER-BLOCK locals across its type switch (nb, hdr2, r2, ep, e, k1 and more per arm), and by claim.law.inner-block-pad-reaches-below-the-compiler-temps inner-block declarations are exactly what occupies the low region the target does not reserve. Hoisting those inner-block declarations to function scope (or collapsing them by dead-local identity reuse, which is what closed sndFxQueAddEx this session) should drain the low region toward target's 16 bytes; the remaining budget after the pad is ~56 bytes, i.e. roughly 14 four-byte declarations. MEASUREMENT RESOLUTION: alias-aware (r1) displacement dump on both sides, calibrated against the five published low_gap values before use; 8-byte ruler response confirmed.
